---
title: "How does it change if we model the fuselage and its mass?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
res = optimize_glider_with_fuse()
sol = res["sol"]

new_sink = sol.value(res["sink_rate"])
new_mass = sol.value(res["mass"])
new_c_root = sol.value(res["c_root"])

old_sink = 0.36
old_mass = 0.00356
old_c_root = 0.0965

c_root_bound = 0.15
```

::: {.hero-pair}
[`{python} f"{old_sink:.2f}"`]{.hero-value}
[m/s sink rate]{.hero-label}

[`{python} f"{new_sink:.2f}"`]{.hero-value}
[with fuselage]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** Adding the fuselage increases the glider's mass, which drives the wing root chord to its maximum bound to carry the extra weight. This keeps the sink rate penalty to a minimum.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified
Asked of the user, 2026-09-14:

1. **Fuselage: 5 mm foam**, doubled up.
2. **Dimensions: 15 mm high, 200 mm long**.
:::

1. **Fuselage width: 10 mm**, doubled 5 mm foam.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print("| Metric | No Fuselage | With Fuselage |")
print("|---|---|---|")
print(f"| Mass (g) | {old_mass * 1000:.1f} | {new_mass * 1000:.1f} |")
print(f"| Root Chord (mm) | {old_c_root * 1000:.0f} | {new_c_root * 1000:.0f} |")
print(f"| Sink Rate (m/s) | {old_sink:.2f} | {new_sink:.2f} |")
print("\n: Comparison of optimized glider parameters.")
```
